disclaimer: Educational decision support only. Similar symptoms can have non-disease causes. Confirm diagnosis with a KVK, agricultural extension officer, or plant pathologist. Use only products registered for the crop and disease locally and follow the current label.

symptoms: Yellow-orange powdery pustules in narrow stripes along leaf veins
Severe infection dries leaves and shrivels grain
prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen and monitor during cool humid weather
treatment: Use a locally registered rust fungicide only when advised; rotate mode-of-action groups
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Scattered round orange-brown pustules mainly on upper leaf surfaces
Leaves yellow and dry when infection is severe
prevention: Use resistant varieties and remove volunteer wheat
Sow at the locally recommended time
treatment: Assess upper-leaf infection before grain filling
Apply a registered rust fungicide only under local advisory
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Elongated reddish-brown pustules on stems, sheaths, and leaves
Late pustules become black; stems may weaken and lodge
prevention: Use resistant varieties and certified seed
Destroy volunteer cereals and report unusual outbreaks
treatment: Use only locally registered fungicides according to surveillance advice
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: The entire ear is replaced by a loose black powder
Spores blow away leaving a bare central rachis
prevention: Use resistant varieties and approved seed treatment
treatment: Remove smutted heads before spores disperse where practical
Do not save grain from affected lots as seed
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Long grey-black stripes under the leaf epidermis
Leaves twist, split, and plants remain stunted
prevention: Use clean treated seed and resistant varieties
Rotate with non-host crops and control volunteer wheat
treatment: Rogue affected plants before spore release
Seek advice on a registered systemic seed treatment for the next sowing
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Only part of a grain becomes black and powdery
Crushed grain may have a fishy odour
prevention: Use certified seed and tolerant varieties
Avoid moving contaminated seed and follow quarantine rules
treatment: No field cure exists for infected grain
Report suspected cases and do not retain affected grain for seed
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails
